chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Safwan al-Jammal who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Had the people known the true nature of how God facilitates bearing (burdens) for the weak, they would not consider any animal expensive.'

key_terms.الضَّعِيف: The weak one; one lacking physical strength to bear heavy burdens
key_terms.بَهِيمَة: A beast of burden; any quadruped animal, here specifically a riding or pack animal
key_terms.حُمْلَان: The act of bearing or carrying loads; figuratively, God's facilitation of burden-bearing for the weak
key_terms.غَالَوْا: To consider something excessively expensive; to place too high a price on something
key_terms.كُنْه: The true nature, depth, or innermost reality of something; the full and complete understanding

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about God's grace in providing animals for the weak?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that God divinely facilitates and eases the carrying of burdens for the weak, meaning that beasts of burden are a mercy from God for those incapable of bearing heavy loads themselves. The implication is that if people truly understood this divine gift — that God causes animals to obediently bear loads for the weak — they would value animals far more highly and not haggle over their price. This hadith is narrated by Safwan al-Jammal, himself a professional camel-driver, which gives the teaching a fitting context.
